_doc: A SERVER'S GAMEPLAY RULES, ITS PRESETS (2026-11-21; src/relay/storage/gameplay_rules.rs reads this file, Server Settings > ADMIN > Gameplay rules offers it, docs/design/server-rules.md says why).
The operator, that day: "Let's make sure the first server we have setup, via united-humanity is the forgiving game mode. I think realistic will be too much for most people."

In a server's shared world every player plays by the server's levels (data/gameplay/levels.json), not their own: the same rules for everyone there. A server's ruleset is one of these presets or Custom (the admin picks each level). `default` is the preset a new server gets.

A preset's `levels` maps a setting id to one of that setting's level ids. A setting a preset does not name plays at the level a new player gets (the setting's `default` in levels.json, the softened one), which is exactly what Forgiving means, so Forgiving names none. Realistic names every setting (a lib test fails when a setting is added to levels.json without a Realistic level here). A setting marked `personal` in levels.json (the bodies' animation: how they are drawn, not a rule of the game) is never the server's: no preset names it.
Each preset's name (`words`) and the sentence saying what it changes (`says`) are keys in data/i18n/en.json.
